title: Add synthetic negation suite and deferred fix queue for prompt regressions
author: Priya Anand
commits: fe2a1b2: add synthetic negation generator and base harness
d4b3c9a: wire up CI hook and deferred fix queue skeleton
a9f7d11: add unit tests and fixtures for negation scenarios
c5b8e20: docs and CI config tweaks
description:
Summary: Adds a targeted synthetic negation test suite and a lightweight deferred-fix queue CI hook to reduce noisy blocking failures while preserving visibility into prompt-set regressions.

Motivation: We frequently see regressions around negation, double-negation, and polarity flips that are under-covered by existing prompt sets. Those failures can be brittle and noisy, leading to frequent CI blocks and alert fatigue. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a synthetic negation suite that programmatically generates diverse negation/contradiction variants across prompt templates, and (2) a deferred-fix queue CI hook that surfaces failing prompt-set checks into a non-blocking queue for triage while still allowing fast-path merges for low-risk changes.

Design:
- Synthetic generator implements a hierarchy of perturbations (single negation, scoped negation, lexical inversion, prefix vs. sentence-level negation) and records deterministic fingerprints for reproducibility.
- Tests include a curated baseline of high-salience prompt templates and a stochastic sampling mode for nightly stress runs.
- CI hook evaluates the negation suite as a separate check. Failures are recorded in the deferred fix queue (backed by a lightweight ledger file checked into artifacts and an optional webhook to the QA Linear project).
- The deferred queue exposes metadata: failing prompts, example model outputs, failure severity (high/medium/low) heuristics based on prior flakiness and semantic distance.

Implementation notes:
- New file eval/harness/suites/synthetic_negation.py contains generator, canonical perturbation pipeline, and deterministic seed handling.
- Deferred queue in eval/harness/ci_hooks/deferred_fix_queue.py implements a pluggable policy: default is 'non-blocking-notify' but maintainers can opt into 'block-on-critical' by label.
- Added unit tests in eval/harness/tests/test_negation_suite.py with fixed seeds to keep CI stable.
- docs/eval/negation-suite.md documents usage, how to add templates, and how to opt a library into stricter gating.

Checklist:
- [x] Synthetic generator with deterministic fingerprinting
- [x] Unit tests and CI integration
- [x] Deferred queue implementation with metadata capture
- [x] Documentation and usage examples
- [x] Linear linkage for triage (QA-4452)

Review summary:
- Ethan: requested that the deferred queue include a short-term retention policy to avoid unbounded ledger growth; implemented via a 90-day TTL and pruning routine (see commit f2e3a44).
- Sophia: asked for tighter test fixtures to avoid flakiness on GPUs with different tokenizers; added tokenizer-agnostic assertions and cross-tokenizer smoke checks.
- Marcus: suggested a severity heuristic threshold to keep the queue actionable; added a simple semantic-distance rule that downgrades micro-diffs to low severity.

CI behavior:
- Unit tests and lint pass on main (all checks green).
- Negation suite runs as a separate check named "negation-suite" and reports results to the CI summary.
- Failing checks create an artifact JSON and append a record to artifacts/deferred_fix_ledger.json (CI only) for maintainers to inspect.

Example changed areas (high-level):
- added new harness module and tests
- wired CI config to run in both PR and nightly modes
- added docs and an example guide for partner teams

Migration/opt-in notes:
- By default the deferred queue is non-blocking; teams can opt into blocking mode by adding the label `eval-blocking` to a PR.
- To add custom templates, drop YAML files under eval/harness/templates/ and register them in the suite manifest.

Related work: This PR complements existing cohort and anchor-based evals by providing targeted perturbation coverage for logical operators and polarity flips.

Linked Linear tickets: ENG-11234 (negation coverage initiative), QA-4452 (deferred triage workflow).

Merge: Squash merge to main after approvals.

Post-merge steps:
- Kick off a 24-hour nightly run in staging with stochastic sampling enabled
- Monitor the deferred_fix_ledger artifact and create QA tasks for high-severity entries.
review_comments: Ethan Li: Deferred queue needs retention - otherwise we'll accumulate thousands of trivial failures.
Priya Anand: Added TTL and pruning routine; ledger rotates daily and prunes >90d entries in maintenance job.
Sophia Chen: Tests were flaky on macOS + HF tokenizers; switched to tokenizer-agnostic evaluation and added a smoke check.
Marcus Park: Suggest adding a semantic-distance fallback for severity - implemented and tuned to avoid noise.
release_notes: Add: Synthetic negation perturbation suite (targeted tests for negation & polarity flips); Add: Deferred-fix queue CI hook to capture non-blocking prompt-set failures; Docs: usage guide and opt-in instructions.
